author: Vitor
notes: Excellent exercise, hard but possible without crazy shenanigans.
aiExplanation: This function solves the problem where every `(` must be closed by a **pair** of `))`, and it counts the minimum number of characters to insert to make the string valid. It walks through the string once, keeping three counters: `open` tracks `(` characters still waiting to be closed, `closed` counts `)` pairs that appear with **no** matching `(` before them (each needs one `(` inserted), and `missing` counts places where a single `)` appears without a second `)` right after it (each needs one `)` inserted). When it sees a `(`, it just increments `open` and moves on. When it sees a `)`, it first tries to match it with a pending `(` by decrementing `open`; if none is available, it bumps `closed` instead. Then it checks whether the **next** character is also `)`: if so, it skips ahead one index because the pair is complete, otherwise it increments `missing`. Finally, it returns `open * 2 + closed + missing`, since every unclosed `(` needs two `)` added, every unmatched `)` pair needs one `(` added, and every lone `)` needs one more `)` added.
